title: $\beta$-ensembles
exact_utf8_statement: Random point processes corresponding to $\beta$-ensembles, or, equivalently, log gases at inverse temperature $\beta$, are defined for arbitrary $\beta>0$. The orthogonal, unitary, and symplectic ensembles corresponding to $\beta=1, 2,$ or 4, respectively, are now, of course, well understood, but other values of $\beta$ are also believed to be relevant in applications, for example, in the statistical description of headway in freeway traffic. For certain rational values of $\beta$, $\beta$-ensembles are related to Jack polynomials, but for general $\beta$ much less is known. The analysis of $\beta$-ensembles for general $\beta$ represents an interesting, and increasingly important, challenge. Recently there have been significant developments in the theory of general $\beta$-ensembles. As a result of the work of Edelman and Dumitriu, and also others, we now know that for all $\beta>0$, there exist (tridiagonal) random matrix models whose eigenvalues are distributed according to $\beta$-ensembles. Furthermore, taking an appropriate scaling limit of these tridiagonal matrix ensembles, one arrives at the following remarkable fact. Let $B(x)$, $x\geq0$, denote Brownian motion, and for any $\beta>0$, let $H_\beta$ denote the Schr\"odinger operator $\frac{d^2}{dx^2}-x-\frac{2}{\sqrt \beta} dB(x)$ acting on $L^2((0,\infty),dx)$ with Dirichlet boundary conditions at $x=0$. Then (Edelman-Sutton, Ramirez-Rider-Virag) for almost all realizations $B(x)$, $x\geq0$, $H_\beta$ is self-adjoint with discrete spectrum $\lambda_1(B,\beta)>\lambda_2(B,\beta)>\cdots$ and for each $k$, $\lambda_k(B,\beta)$ has precisely the same distribution as the $k^th$ largest eigenvalues of the corresponding $\beta$-ensemble in the standard edge scaling limit. Part of the challenge in analyzing general $\beta$-ensembles is to use $H_\beta$ to obtain information about these ensembles. Already the variational characterization of the $\lambda_k$'s has been used to give simple proofs of bounds on the asymptotics of the distributions of the $\lambda_k$'s. Question: can one derive the Tracy-Widom formula for $\lambda_1(B;\beta=2)$, say, directly from $H_\beta$? At a more conceptual level, the ($\beta$-ensemble $\leftrightarrow H_\beta$) correspondence brings random matrix theory front and center into the arena and practice of modern day probability theory.
quantifiers_and_scope_review: The concrete subquestion is direct beta=2 Tracy-Widom derivation from the stochastic Airy operator, amid a broad research program. Requires operator-domain and Brownian-potential definitions; merely importing ensemble equivalence is not a direct derivation. Successor bodies not checked.

quantifiers_and_scope_review: One absolute positive c for every integer a>=2, nearest-integer norm of natural log. Primary Conjecture2.14 matches and explains product-log versus sum-log obstruction. Pointwise transcendence gives nonzero distances, not this uniform polynomial lower bound.

title: Conjecture 5.4 — Loxton and van der Poorten
exact_utf8_statement:
Let $(n_i)_{i\ge 0}$ be an
increasing sequence of positive integers. Assume there is a prime

$$

$$
\sum_{i\ge 0}10^{-n_i}
$$
is transcendental.

Read primary Conjecture5.4 and successor Theorem7. Indicator digits are 0/1, so no carries or p-reduction ambiguity; irrational series forbids eventual periodicity; Theorems2/7 apply with base10. title: Probabilistic McMillan theorem in higher dimensions
exact_utf8_statement: Let $X_t$ be $d$-dimensional Brownian motion starting at the origin, let $D$ be an open subset of $\mathbb{R}^d$ containing the origin, and let $\tau=\inf\{t>0:X_t\notin D\}$. Let $A$ be the set of cluster points of $$(X_t-X_\tau)/|X_t-X_\tau|$$ as $t \uparrow \tau$. For every $d>2$ and every such $D$, is $A$ almost surely either a sphere or a hemisphere?
quantifiers_and_scope_review: Every d>2 and every open D containing0. Literal allows infinite exit time; then X_tau and directions are undefined. Sphere/hemisphere conclusion for finite exits still requires fine boundary analysis; excluded endpoint/domain correction earns no credit.

title: Topology of planar Brownian trace
exact_utf8_statement: Let $X_t$ be two-dimensional Brownian motion. (i) For every pair $x,y \notin X[0,1]$, is there a Jordan arc $\Gamma$ containing $x$ and $y$ such that $\Gamma\cap X[0,1]$ is finite? (ii) If $\{A_k\}_{k\ge1}$ are the connected components of $\mathbb{R}^2\setminus X[0,1]$ and $K=X[0,1]\setminus\bigcup_{k\ge1}\partial A_k$, is $K$ totally disconnected?
quantifiers_and_scope_review: Two distinct assertions for planar Brownian trace: finite-intersection Jordan arcs for every complementary pair and total disconnectedness of buried points. A proof of one does not resolve both; universal random topology needs substantial continuum arguments.

title: Non-extinction of a Fleming–Viot particle model
exact_utf8_statement: Let $N$ particles move as independent Brownian motions in a bounded connected open set $D\subset\mathbb{R}^d$. Whenever a particle hits the complement of $D$, replace it by a copy of a uniformly chosen surviving particle. If $\tau_k$ is the time of the $k$th death-and-branching event and $\tau_\infty=\lim_{k\to\infty}\tau_k$, is $\tau_\infty=\infty$ almost surely for every such $D$?
quantifiers_and_scope_review: All bounded connected open D, every particle system under intended N>=2. N=1 has no survivor and simultaneous deaths need conventions. Smooth-boundary nonexplosion does not establish irregular domains; no full coupling/Lyapunov control.

title: Do peaks of random labelings repel each other?
exact_utf8_statement: Choose uniformly a bijective labeling of the vertices of the $n\times n$ discrete square by $1,2,\ldots,n^2$, and call a vertex a peak when all adjacent vertices have lower labels. Condition on there being exactly two peaks, and let $\rho_n$ be their graph distance. Does $\rho_n/n$ converge in distribution to $0$ as $n\to\infty$?
quantifiers_and_scope_review: Condition on exactly two peaks and show rescaled graph distance tends to0 in law. Title's repel wording is opposite the literal concentration direction; do not silently replace it by macroscopic separation. Needs primary scope before combinatorial enumeration.

title: Constant-factor online scheduling of subadditive batches
exact_utf8_statement: Tasks arrive as a rate-one Poisson process and have types in $[0,1]$; batch processing time $S$ is monotone and strictly subadditive and type $a$ incurs waiting cost rate $c(a)$. Is there an explicit online algorithm and universal constant $C$ whose long-run average cost $W$ satisfies $W/W_*<C$ for every $S$ and $c$ whenever the optimal value $W_*$ is finite?
quantifiers_and_scope_review: One online algorithm and universal constant for all monotone strictly-subadditive batch costs and all type waiting costs with finite optimum. Input distribution, information model and zero-optimum division need definitions; a fixed batching rule cannot be asserted universally competitive.

title: Exact coupling of singular non-discrete random walks

Suppose the step lengths are neither discrete nor spread out. For which initial positions $x$ can the walks be coupled so that $S_n=S'_n$ for every sufficiently large $n$ almost surely?
quantifiers_and_scope_review: All starting offsets x classified for a common singular non-discrete non-spread-out step law. Eventual exact equality is stronger than approximate or distributional coupling; support-difference conditions alone do not establish successful finite-time coalescence.

title: Setwise convergence versus total-variation convergence of shifted processes

If $\mathbb{P}(\theta_nX\in A)\to\mathbb{P}(X'\in A)$ for every measurable path-space set $A$, must $\mathbb{P}(\theta_nX\in\cdot)$ converge to $\mathbb{P}(X'\in\cdot)$ in total variation?
quantifiers_and_scope_review: Setwise convergence on the entire measurable path sigma-field of shifts, not finite-dimensional marginals, must imply TV. Oscillating density examples for arbitrary measures need realization as a single shift orbit; no valid shift-orbit construction established.

title: Coupling characterization of setwise asymptotic stationarity

quantifiers_and_scope_review: Conditional on failure of the preceding implication, seek a characterization for all measurable path sets. A Skorokhod weak-convergence representation does not characterize setwise convergence, and a counterexample alone is not this characterization.

title: Conjecture 0.1 — Is there an infinite expander?
exact_utf8_statement: Call an infinite connected graph $G$ of uniformly bounded degree an infinite expander if there is a constant $c>0$ such that, for every vertex set $S$ and every finite-radius ball $B(r)$ satisfying $|S\cap B(r)|<|B(r)|/2$, one has $|\partial S\cap B(r)|>c|S\cap B(r)|$, where $\partial S$ is the vertex boundary of $S$. Prove that no infinite expander exists.
quantifiers_and_scope_review: All bounded-degree infinite connected graphs, one c for every S and ball. Empty S makes strict0>0 fail literally; trivial wording refutation excluded. Under intended positive intersections, ordinary Cheeger expansion is not uniform expansion inside every ball; parked substantive scope.

title: Equilibrium point configurations on the line
exact_utf8_statement: Let $(a_n)_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}$ be a locally finite configuration of points on $\mathbb{R}$. For the force law $F(x,y)=|x-y|^{-2}$, call the configuration an equilibrium if $$\sum_{i\ne n}|a_i-a_n|^{-2}\operatorname{sgn}(a_i-a_n)=0$$ for every $n$. quantifiers_and_scope_review: All locally finite bi-infinite configurations and force balance at every point. Need increasing indexing and absolute summation convention; permuting a lattice only exploits omitted ordering. Maximum-gap comparison needs an attained extremum or compactness; local finiteness alone gives neither uniform gaps nor global force control.
